title: Riders Left Short of Their Destination: Stranding Shares on Wayfare Rides
content:
In a wrong drop-off review on **Wayfare Rides (rider trips and fares)**, the stranding share follows how far short the rider was left. Two records decide it: the trip's estimated miles against its actual miles, and whether the rider was charged for a **Wayfare Bikes and Scooters** ride (a Wayfare Bikes ride charge) on the charge date of the trip's fare charge.

**Rule.** Where the trip's actual miles fall short of its estimated miles by at least the short drop-off miles of 1.5 miles, and the rider was charged for at least one Wayfare Bikes ride on the charge date of the fare charge, the share is the stranded-by-bike share of 0.45. Where the actual miles fall short by at least 1.5 miles and no Wayfare Bikes ride was charged on that date, the share is the stranded share of 0.30. Otherwise the stranding share is not changed by how short the drop-off was.

The shortfall is the estimated miles less the actual miles.

## Truth table

| Shortfall of at least 1.5 miles | Wayfare Bikes ride charged on the fare charge date | Stranding share |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes (one or more) | 0.45 |
| Yes | No | 0.30 |
| No | Yes | not changed |
| No | No | not changed |

## Either side of the 1.5-mile line (hypothetical trips)

- Estimated 6.0 miles, actual 4.5 miles: short by 1.5 miles — at least 1.5, so the trip counts as short. With a Wayfare Bikes ride charged that day the share is 0.45; without one, 0.30.
- Estimated 6.0 miles, actual 4.6 miles: short by 1.4 miles — not short enough; a Wayfare Bikes ride that day does not change the share.
- Actual miles above the estimated miles: no shortfall at all.
